subject: SIG: escrow attestation and process for prompt exclusion / audit snapshot
messages:
From: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@medixhealth.com>
To: Grace Occonnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Medix Health Compliance <compliance@medixhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: attestation + escrow snapshot for prompt exclusion

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our SIG intake and procurement checklist, our security team needs two items before we can proceed to procurement:

1) A signed attestation confirming that Medix Health customer prompts and chat content will not be used for model retraining or persistent model updates unless explicitly opted into via contract.
2) A snapshot/archive (read-only) of the current logging configuration and a short audit artifact showing where ephemeral prompt logs are stored, retention TTLs, and the mechanism to exclude specific accounts from any training pipelines.

Can you confirm what you can provide and approximate delivery timelines?

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Bennett
Head of Compliance
Medix Health

From: Grace Occonnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@medixhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: attestation + escrow snapshot for prompt exclusion

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the note. We can provide both items. High-level plan and deliverables below:

Deliverables
- Signed attestation PDF (legal + security) stating that customer prompts are excluded from model training unless contractually allowed.
- Evidence snapshot (zip) containing: logging config exports, TTL settings for prompt/kv caches, the data flow diagram showing ephemeral stores, and an export of the audit-run (read-only) that demonstrates a sample account exclusion.
- Short runbook describing how customers can opt-out (API flags + console controls) and how we operationalize exclusions in the serving runtime.

Timeline
- Draft attestation and runbook: EOD Tue 10 Aug (we will send as a DocuSign envelope for signature).
- Evidence snapshot (redacted where necessary) and logging exports: Wed 11 Aug noon PT.

Notes on scope
- Our default behavior is ephemeral prefix/KV caches with TTLs configured per-account; these caches are not used for offline model retraining. Persistent logs used for debugging (access logs, error logs) are retained per the customer contract and our retention matrix — we will include the exact retention entries for Medix in the snapshot.
- For customers wanting an additional contractual assurance, we provide a standard training exclusion clause and can lock that into the account-level org settings on Dedicated/Private deployments or as an addendum for Hosted with an agreed scope.

I’ll loop in Marcus and Soojin to confirm the artifacts and we’ll upload everything to a restricted Drive folder.

Best,
Grace
Grace O'Connor
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@medixhealth.com>
To: Grace Occonnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Medix Health Compliance <compliance@medixhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: attestation + escrow snapshot for prompt exclusion

Grace —

Thanks, that sounds good. A couple quick clarifications from our security team so we can scope the audit artifact correctly:

- For the "ephemeral prefix/KV caches" you mention, can you confirm typical TTL ranges (e.g., seconds/minutes/hours) and whether TTLs are configurable per-customer?
- For the "not used for offline model retraining" statement, we need a brief technical explanation of the safeguards (e.g., access controls, pipeline gating, logs exclusion) that ensure prompt data cannot reach training pipelines.
- If you plan to include redacted samples in the evidence snapshot, please confirm the redaction method and attest that no customer-identifiable data will be included.

If you can answer inline, we can triage the DocuSign step quickly.

Regards,
Sarah

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@medixhealth.com>, Grace Occonnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2026 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: attestation + escrow snapshot for prompt exclusion

Hi Sarah — following up with the specifics requested. Grace asked me to provide the technical clarifications below; I’ve attached the attestation and the evidence snapshot to the Drive link and sent the DocuSign envelope to the email on file.

1) TTLs and configurability
- Typical default TTLs: prefix/KV cache default = 60s for hot prefixes; session-level ephemeral cache = 5 minutes; specialized short-term request cache = 15s.
- TTLs are configurable per-customer for Dedicated and Private customers via config profiles. For Hosted customers we offer org-level flags and can set account-specific overrides with an SLA/commitment. We included the exact TTL settings applied historically for Medix Health in the audit snapshot (audit_snapshot-20260810/logging-config.json).

2) Safeguards preventing prompt data from entering training pipelines
- Isolation: The training pipelines are isolated from the inference runtime by network ACLs and a dedicated ingestion service. No direct ingress from production inference logs into training storage is permitted.
- Pipeline gating: Any dataset construction for training requires an approval ticket and automated checks; the training ingestion service ignores any table/stream tagged as "ephemeral".
- Access controls & separation: Only the research team has credentials for the training clusters; those credentials are managed via short-lived certificates and recorded in audit logs.
- Offline storage: Persistent debug logs are stored in a customer-scoped bucket with retention controls; raw prompt cache dumps are not persisted to the training buckets.

3) Redaction and sample artifacts
- Redaction method: We perform deterministic field-level redaction using the same pipeline used for support exports — PII fields (names, emails, SSNs) are replaced with token shards and original hashes are stored only in a separate HSM-backed service for correlation (never exposed).
- Attestation: The evidence snapshot includes only redacted artifacts; no customer-identifiable data is included. You’ll find a short redaction report in the snapshot (redaction-report.txt).

Next steps we completed
- Uploaded evidence to restricted Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-medix-evidence
- DocuSign envelope sent: https://docusign.com/envelope/12345-escrow-attestation
- We flagged Medix’s account for the "training exclusion" tag internally; if you sign the attestation we’ll set the account-level lock and generate an immutable audit entry.

If you want a short 20-minute call to walk a technical reviewer through the artifacts, Soojin and I are available tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Head of Product, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
